Automatic Execution Paths

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential theft:** docs/credentials.md documents Claude Code credential file paths, but it explicitly defines whitelist/redaction rules and states that tokens must not be read or emitted. The ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 reference in config/templates/ssh.yaml is an optional SSH configuration example, not evidence of broad key harvesting or exfiltration.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** No evidence was found of archive staging, temporary collection of harvested files, or uploads to webhooks/C2/raw IP/drop services.
  • **Persistence:** Mentions of systemd, cron, and launchd appear in 05_resource-heartbeat.md as operational documentation for a heartbeat collector. There is no evidence that the package automatically installs services or cron jobs. README/SLURM docs also state that persistent daemons are not installed.
  • **Lateral movement:** SSH/SLURM/remote execution are documented agent-orchestration features. No evidence was found of CI token theft, Kubernetes service-account abuse, Docker socket theft, or cloud metadata access.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** No evidence was found of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec loaders, obfuscated payloads, downloader stubs, or staged malware.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Two PNG files were detected as high-entropy binaries, but README/PKG-INFO reference them as logo/icon documentation assets, which appears normal.
  • From the provided metadata, dependencies such as a2a-sdk, click, pyyaml, rich, uvicorn, and scitex-container do not show clear evidence of typosquatting, sudden malicious dependency insertion, hidden native binaries, or sdist/wheel mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed
